title: A convention, not an unfinished proof
quote: dont le choix reste ... à convention (deux choix possibles)
body: The page explicitly leaves two possible functorial orientation conventions and then specifies first rather than last for the distinguished point. This records dependence on a convention, not a claim that the sign-character calculation has failed; C64-N05 explains the distinction and Hua’s §1 retains it.

title: Three cube correspondences and a canonical orientation are requested
quote: en fait ce cube est canoniquement orienté ; cf plus bas (007); Il y aurait lieu d’expliciter (023–024); orientation canonique (024)
body: The first forward reference is on007, where the cube is called canonically oriented with cf plus bas. The request on023–024 covers vertices versus order-three rotations, opposite-edge pairs versus reflections, faces versus circular permutations, and an orientation construction. Faces are already identified with circular permutations in023’s definition, and the parity-torsor argument reaches OK on025, but the other requested correspondences are not expanded into explicit conversion maps. Hua’s §4 and C64-N16–N19 provide the comparison without attributing the supplementary orbit calculations to the manuscript.

title: Distinguishing authorial reservations from editorial doubts
quote: No clear standalone à vérifier, sauf erreur, je présume or admis located in this packet
body: The confidently legible text contains the reservations and unfinished requests listed above, with no separate legible step introduced by one of those four formulas. Editorial unsure and illegible markers are the transcriber’s doubts and must not be counted as Grothendieck’s own question marks; in particular the doubtful035 margin prevents an absolute claim about every unread word. Contextual occurrences of sauf erreur in LM140-3 scan025 and postponed checks at177 belong to those other texts, not to this packet.
